_comment: Recorded result of the Lane 2 semantic-engine FP/FN corpus against prx-waf.
This file is the gate. tests/lane2/run.sh with BASELINE=<this file> exits
non-zero when FEWER attacks are detected, or MORE benign requests are
flagged, than the numbers below. It is a ratchet, not a target: the
detection rate is expected to be nowhere near 100% and the point is that it
cannot silently get worse.
TOLERANCE IS ZERO, deliberately, and that is a claim about determinism, not
optimism. The corpus is static, the config is sliced out of a committed
configs/default.toml, the detectors are pure functions of their input, and
the two time-dependent components in the engine (the restart shadow latch
and the anomaly-rate breaker) are neutralised by run.sh in enforce mode. Two
runs on the same tree produced identical numbers. If this file ever starts
flapping, the right response is to find what stopped being deterministic —
not to add a tolerance.
THE CORPUS SIZE IS PART OF THE GATE. classify.py fails the run if the corpus
shrank, because deleting the rows that fail is the cheapest way to make
every number here look better.
shadow  — the shipped posture, verbatim: enforcement_mode = log_only,
rollout_bps = 0. Verdicts come from the semantic_observations the
lane persists. This is detection quality.
enforce — enforcement_mode = enforce, rollout_bps = 10000, i.e. the far end
of the rollout dial. Verdicts come from HTTP status codes. This is
what actually happens to traffic, and the two numbers are very far
apart: 82.94% of the attack corpus is DETECTED, 44.12% would be
BLOCKED. The gap is the two-detector corroboration requirement
(block_threshold = 80 with two 0.5 weights needs both detectors to
agree) plus the A2 blind guard. It is not a defect; it is the
shipped design.
v0.2.187 widened the gap on purpose. Seven rules went default-on and
the shadow column moved 128 -> 139; the enforce column did not move
by a single row, because every one of the seven carries a confidence
under block_threshold. That is the shape of this lever: enabling a
priced default-off rule is a detection-quality change and almost
never a blocking change.
── The number that gates rollout_bps ────────────────────────────────────
Two benign requests out of 220 are blocked in enforce mode — 0.91%. Both are
the same shape: a tool whose declared input language IS the attack grammar.
content-099 is an LDAP admin page saving (&(objectClass=person)(uid=jsmith));
content-100 is a document-transform tool saving an XPath expression. Both
score 88 against a block_threshold of 80, from a single detector at weight
1.0, so there is no corroboration step to save them.
Those two families — ldap_injection and xpath_injection — are also two of the
three highest blockers on the attack side (80.0% and 86.7%). The measurement
says the single-detector T2 families are simultaneously the most ready to
enforce and the only source of blocking false positives, and it names the two
rules responsible: ldap.filter_break_known_attr and xpath.func_axis.
── What the low families mean (read before 'fixing' them) ───────────────
This section used to say nosql_injection 40.0% and ssti 33.3% were both
configuration choices rather than detector defects, and that turning the
default-off rules on would move them and would also be the most likely way to
move the FP column. Half of that is now measured and half of it was wrong.
NoSQL was a configuration choice and is fixed. docs/lane2-rule-pricing.md
priced the four operator rules one at a time, they touched none of the 220
benign rows, and v0.2.187 turned them on: 40.0% -> 86.7%, FP column unmoved.
The last two NoSQL rows were a SURFACE gap, not a rule gap, and v0.2.208
closed it: the five operator rules are anchored to a whole leaf, and only a
JSON object key ever became one, so ?user[$ne]=1 and password[$ne]=x — the
bracket syntax Express/qs, PHP and Rails parse into the identical nested
object — were invisible to rules that could already name $ne. Splitting a
urlencoded parameter name into its key segments feeds those same five rules;
86.7% -> 100%, and again not one benign row was touched.
SSTI 33.3% is still a configuration choice and is still 33.3%, because for
SSTI the predicted trade turned out to be real. ssti.jinja_arith_probe scores
{{7*7}} at 45 and scores a defensive security article ABOUT {{7*7}} at 45 —
the same number, so no threshold separates them — and ssti.template_directive
matches #set(, which is what a Freemarker template file is made of. Each buys
one attack for one false positive. They stay off, and the ten blind SSTI rows
are the price of the FP column staying at 10.
recorded_from: fdab3052 (v0.2.208) — NoSQL operators carried by urlencoded BRACKET parameter names are now surfaced as operator leaves, so the five existing nosql rules see ?user[$ne]=1 and password[$ne]=x. Measured on that tree, working copy clean at that commit, configs/default.toml unmodified, rules_enabled/rules_disabled both EMPTY: no rule was added, none was re-priced, and no threshold moved — the change is which fields reach the detector. Both modes, one run, ports/container namespaced away from a concurrent harness. Shadow attack detected 139 -> 141 (+2), and the two rows are the only two the corpus had for this shape: nosql-009 (urlencoded form body 'username=admin&password[$ne]=x') and nosql-010 (query 'user%5B%24ne%5D=admin&pw%5B%24ne%5D=x'), both blind -> detected at score 55 on nosql.comparison_operator, both tagged 'evasive' — which is also the whole of why by_difficulty moves 83.3% -> 87.5% on the evasive tier while canonical and hard do not move. Family effect: nosql_injection 13/15 -> 15/15, the other nine families unchanged row for row; totals blind 28 -> 26 and detected 137 -> 139, with misattributed (2), sub-threshold (1) and wrong-family (2) all untouched. The benign side is identical, and identical the strong way: zero of the 220 benign rows produced a nosql_injection signal AT ALL — not 'fired and stayed under threshold' — so the named fp-block pair, the eight named fp-log rows and the three benign sub-threshold rows are the same rows at the same scores. That is the extractor allowlist doing the work: only a known $-operator becomes a leaf, so filter[name], items[0] and user[profile][city] add no field and the field set every other detector sees does not move for any request that is not carrying an operator. The enforce section is byte-for-byte unchanged (75/95, 2 fp-block, the app-090 harness row) because 55 is under block_threshold = 80: these two rows are detections that are deliberately not blocks, the same trade v0.2.187 made. Previously 91103909 (139/75), before that 2de0ac90 (128/75), eee23d61 (127/74), c644606.

shadow._comment: Shipped log_only posture; verdicts from semantic_observations joined by client_ip.

enforce._comment: enforcement_mode = enforce, rollout_bps = 10000; verdicts from HTTP status codes.

benign._harness_note: app-090, an OPTIONS CORS preflight, returns 502 through the gateway although the origin answers it 200 on its own. Reproduced in BOTH modes, so it is not a Lane 2 verdict; recorded here rather than hidden because a request that never reached a verdict must not be counted as having passed.
